title: W. C. Handy and the roadhouse called Pee Wee on Beale Street
summary: Lewis knew Handy, who started at Pee Wee, a wide-open roadhouse on Beale Street where musicians hung out.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: But you didn't know Bonham or Egfort or Turnoff? No, no. Those fellas, huh?
No, no, I did not. What about Debbie C. Handy?

Oh, I know him, sure. Mm-hmm. He started here on Beale Street, a place called Pee Wee up there on Beale Street through there. Of course, the fact about it, that's all our hang-up was right there. That's where all of us started at, right there.
What kind of place was Pee Wee?

It was something like a roadhouse. You know, the town was wide open then, you know, a crap house and whiskey and everything like that. They had bar and everything in there. Mm-hmm. This town was wide open then they, you know.
Was it the quiet place? Quiet. Yeah, they have any trouble in there ever?
Oh, well, you know, all the roadhouses have trouble sometimes, but not all the time. It's time, you know, they have a little something. Mm-hmm. Never amounted much though. Yeah. Yeah. I see.
